structure:
A single short Markdown ruling file, 60 lines (workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-ian-2026-11-25.md), from Ian, dated 25 November 2026, on pagination of the address book's lists and the party pickers, raised by the manage-notifications pre-flight when registering ruling:paul-2026-11-05 surfaced a conflict with ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 over req-611. It is laid out as: a one-paragraph framing of what raised it; the owner's words as a two-line block quote ("Pagination should be kept. We want it. It was removed previously in error. We actually fixed that theme removing it with a bug EUDPA-827"), which is the ruling proper and the only verbatim source; a "What was asked" section setting the two opposed readings of req-611 side by side as two bullets (Paul's point 8 and Ian's 23 November point 6, the latter quoted); and a "Decided" section of five numbered points, the second carrying three indented code-citation bullets naming address book files (RequestedListFilters.java, AddressController.java, ListPaging.java) and a closing paragraph of reasoning. After point 5 comes an unnumbered closing paragraph marked as the orchestrator's call, applying the ruling and explicitly open to being overruled, on the plants contact picker's page size moving from five to eight, citing insfrontend:src/server/app/features/address-book/list/list.controller.js:49 and REQ-INS-ADDR-013. Scope is the whole file and nothing is left out. At 60 lines it is far inside one agent's reading, so it is one part.

Extracted in 1 part:
Part 1, Whole ruling: Part 1, "Whole ruling": the whole of workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-ian-2026-11-25.md, read in full (65 lines). Laid out as: a one-paragraph framing naming what raised the ruling (the manage-notifications pre-flight, where registering ruling:paul-2026-11-05 surfaced a conflict with ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 over req-611); the owner's words as a two-line block quote, which is the ruling proper; a "What was asked" section putting the two opposed readings of req-611 side by side as two bullets (Paul's point 8, and Ian's 23 November point 6 quoted); and a "Decided" section of six numbered points — point 2 carrying three indented code-citation bullets on the address book (RequestedListFilters.java, AddressController.java, ListPaging.java) and a closing paragraph of reasoning, and point 6 carrying a second block quote confirming the page size. Covered: the framing; the owner's block quote (pagination kept, wanted, removed in error, the removing theme fixed by bug EUDPA-827); both readings of req-611; decided point 1 (every address book list and every address picker pages, no unpaginated requirement); point 2 (req-611's 'unpaginated' clause dropped, ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 superseded on that point alone, the three code citations and the role-filter-before-the-page reasoning, Paul's point 8 standing in full); point 3 (the rest of the 23 November ruling stands: pickers at eight, inc-087 criteria 7-9's one-page clause and req-594/req-595 stay dropped, the "Selected address" restatement returns with the paging); point 4 (EUDPA-827 landed: animals-frontend 0d1d606d merged to main on 24 November with workspace 1ec8d9b7, live animals pickers need no further work); point 5 (conflict c-292 settled, the plants contact picker keeps its pagination and 'Selected address' inset and takes req-1964); and point 6 (the plants contact picker pages at eight not five, matching the INS address book list's figure, asked as an orchestrator's call and confirmed by Ian the same day). Four gap claims record what the ruling leaves open on what it touches. Note on the partition: its "covers" expects the page-size decision to sit in an unnumbered orchestrator's-call paragraph, open to being overruled, with the plants contact picker's five-or-eight recorded as a gap. The file as read has moved on: that paragraph is now numbered point 6 and carries Ian's own confirmation ("contact picker should be 8 yes"), so it is recorded as a decision, verbatim, with the orchestrator's-call origin kept as its own claim, and no gap is raised on it.

The ruling says the live animals pickers need no further work and that the plants contact picker's page size changes, but does not say whether anywhere else the pagination was removed from still needs work.
